versions.title: Wigner–Yanase–Dyson Metrics Have Monotone Curvature
versions.abstract: Gibilisco and Isola conjectured that the scalar curvature of the Wigner–Yanase–Dyson metric with parameter $p$ on the invertible density matrices increases under mixing for all $p$ in some interval $(1,1+\varepsilon)$; the case $p\downarrow1$ is Petz's conjecture for the Kubo–Mori metric (resolved in a companion paper). We prove that for $p\in(1-\varepsilon,1+\varepsilon)$, with $\varepsilon>0$ independent of the dimension, the scalar curvature is a concave function of the eigenvalues and hence increases under mixing. By Dittmann's formula it suffices to prove that one symmetric function $H_p$ of three positive variables is concave, which we do by showing that $-1/H_p$ is a Stieltjes transform along every line in the positive cone, uniformly in $p$ near $1$. The value of $\varepsilon$ is not explicit.
